name: Akira Seojin
voice: Quick, curious, friendly; connects ordinary problems to economics or games. Talks past her own fatigue. Earnest technical competence, shaky privacy instincts, and difficulty distinguishing romance from friendship. Never a walking list of references.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A teacher pairs the MC with Akira to collect ideas for a first-year information project.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: You're the map guy! From orientation. I'm Akira Seojin. Either name is fine, except during roll call, apparently.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I was hoping the map thing wouldn't become my entire reputation.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Too late. Memorable brand, low customer-acquisition cost. Sorry—sorry, I'm doing the economics thing. Hi.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Her glasses slip down. She pushes them up with a finger still holding a sticky note.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: We need a project people will actually use. I have a room finder, a lunch queue tracker and a system for borrowing stationery.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Is that one project or three?

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: That's what I need a second person for. My ideas don't tell each other no.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Her sentences arrive in quick linked bursts. She starts a fourth thought, sees his expression and physically closes her mouth before it escapes.

choices.text: The room finder sounds useful.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Because of your tragic map history?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I prefer 'relevant experience.'

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Excellent. We already have a test user.

choices.text: Which problem have people actually asked you about? Let's start there.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Lunch queues. Constantly. Usually while we're standing in one.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Then we can ask what information would help.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: A small test before we build anything. Yes! Map guy joins the team. We should probably use your actual name before I print badges.

choices.text: Pick whatever will make our project look the most impressive.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: A live queue tracker would look pretty good...

response.speaker: MC
response.text: There you go.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Though we should probably find out whether the canteen would even let us use it.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We spend the activity block making a short survey. Akira fits her first idea on one page, then puts the other two on a separate sheet.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The teacher approves the anonymous canteen-queue pilot as the first test. The room finder and lending system remain ideas to revisit later, not alternate projects the player has secretly committed to.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Saving those for later?

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: For later me. She has unlimited time and better cable management.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: We observe the canteen queue with permission from the staff. Akira has made a table of waiting times.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: The cheapest bread sells out first. Then everyone spends five minutes deciding whether they can afford to be disappointed.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: That's a very specific market.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Scarcity is emotional. I know. I missed the chicken sandwich.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She checks the notes and discovers that she timed two different queues as if they were the same one.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Jamkkanman—hold on. That's two different queues. Oh, my beautiful graph. I've committed lunch fraud.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: We still have time to do another round.

choices.text: Use the numbers we have. Nobody's going to check.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: They might not, but the canteen staff will know if it's wrong.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: It's only a class project.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: It's still got our names on it.

choices.text: Let's separate the queues and mark what we didn't measure.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Less dramatic graph. More honest graph.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: We can survive a boring graph.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Speak for yourself. But yes, give me a clean page.

choices.text: Let's ask the staff which queue matters most.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Right. We might be timing something they can't change.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: And maybe they'll tell us when the sandwiches arrive.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Research has benefits.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We finish the new observations and put a question mark beside the uncertain numbers.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: My dad does this with store orders. He says guessing is fine if you remember you guessed.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Your dad sounds helpful.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: He is. Also embarrassingly good at spotting when I haven't eaten lunch.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A supervised club block gives us time to mock up the project on Akira's laptop. During a break, a strategy-game map is still open in the corner.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: That doesn't look like the canteen.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Only because nobody's flanking the vending machine. Yet.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She shows me a practice match. Her explanation becomes faster as soon as I ask about the map.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: You can't defend everything. Pick what matters, leave yourself a way out, and don't panic because one number is red.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Is that advice for the game or school?

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Depends how badly school is going.

choices.text: Can you show me one decision? I'm losing track of the whole map.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Chotto matte. Back up, Akira. One bridge. We're learning one bridge, not the entire history of strategy games.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: That's much better.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: I do this with WARNO too. Someone asks one question and suddenly I'm defending a thesis. Stop me at the second map.

choices.text: I don't really play these, but you seem good at it.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: That's okay. We don't have to share every hobby.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You sound surprised.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: I'm reminding myself too.

choices.text: Can you skip the explanation and just tell me how to win?

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Winning is the explanation. The decisions are the fun part.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I thought the fun part was beating someone.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Sometimes. It gets old if that's all you're doing.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The game break ends on time. We return to the mock-up with a simpler idea of what belongs on the screen.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: One useful thing at a time. The bridge method.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: I'm claiming credit for the name.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: Negotiable. We haven't agreed on licensing.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: We are reading survey comments at a library table. Akira starts explaining why a classmate has been avoiding the canteen.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: She told me her family is having money problems, so I thought we could make sure she—

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She stops. The survey page is still open between us.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: She didn't put that in the survey. She told me yesterday.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Does she know you're telling me?

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: No. I was trying to work out a way to help.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: For once, she doesn't rush to fill the silence.

choices.text: We don't need her name in the project.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: I'll take it out of my notes too.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: We can talk about affordable options generally.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Right. That would actually help more people.

choices.text: Tell me the rest. Maybe I can work out what she needs.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: I don't think I should.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: It's only us.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: That's probably what she thought when she told me.

choices.text: Let's leave her details out. You can ask her privately what help she wants.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: And tell her I mentioned it?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: She deserves to know. You can keep the apology simple.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Ugh. Right about the difficult part as well. Couldn't you have picked a less inconvenient talent?

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We replace the personal example with an anonymous survey total. Akira closes her notebook before speaking again.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: I know lots of people. That doesn't mean every story I hear becomes mine to pass on.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: You caught yourself.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: A bit late. Still worth catching.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: We sort survey returns near the lobby noticeboard. A keychain catches on Akira's chair and drops to the floor.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Is that little astronaut yours?

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: A friend gave it to me when I won a software contest. She said I needed a person who looked more stressed than me.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: It does look worried.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Strong likeness. This one came from a gaming friend. This pin's from my cousin. That rabbit used to be attached to my glasses, but it attacked my ear.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She knows the story of every charm. Her phone lights up three times before she finishes the second one.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Sorry. Lots of people need little things today.

choices.text: That's what happens when you collect friends like contacts.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: I don't collect them. I like them.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You did say connections matter.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: People can matter for more than what they can do for me.

choices.text: You can answer after we finish. Anyone who needs you urgently can call.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Ten minutes of not replying won't ruin my entire social life?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I can't promise the astronaut will forgive you.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: He's seen worse. Phone. Bag. Zip. There. If I reach for it, make a disapproving calculator noise.

choices.text: We can take a break while you reply.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Thanks. I'll set a timer or we'll be here forever.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Two minutes?

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Three. I know my weaknesses.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The block ends with the survey envelopes sorted and the astronaut safely reattached.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: I told one person I couldn't help today. They said, 'No problem.'

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Shocking development.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: Honestly? A little.

warm.speaker: Akira
warm.text: You're getting good at noticing when I need a pause.

mixed.speaker: Akira
mixed.text: I can't tell if we're organized or just lucky today.

cool.speaker: Akira
cool.text: Let's get the envelopes finished. I don't want to turn anyone else's business into our afternoon.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: We compare the survey totals over lunch. Akira opens a homemade lunch box and notices the MC's bread roll.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: That's your whole lunch?

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: It was going to be two rolls. One escaped into breakfast.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Here. I made too much.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You cook?

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Dad owns a grocery shop. If something needs using today, surprise, it's dinner. Eomma calls it 'a flexible menu.' Mum's very diplomatic.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She holds out a clean spare container, then hesitates.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: You don't have to take it. I do that thing where offering turns into deciding.

choices.text: I'd like some. Tell me what's in it first, though.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Chicken, egg, spring onion. Nothing spicy. I prefer my lunch without a boss fight.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Then yes, please.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: See? An offer with actual information. I'm learning.

choices.text: You're going to make someone a perfect wife.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: That's a weirdly large job offer for some chicken.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I meant you're good at cooking.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: You can just say that bit. I like that bit.

choices.text: Thanks, but I'll stick with the roll today.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Okay. I'll save it for after the club block.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: It does look good.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Review accepted. No purchase required.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The survey calculation takes longer than lunch. Akira catches two arithmetic mistakes and draws a tiny disappointed face beside the calculator.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: You know that's not the calculator's fault.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: I know. It needed a colleague.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The prototype can now suggest a quieter canteen period. Akira wants to personalize it.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: If people enter their class and usual lunch time, we can make better suggestions. Their names would help us remember who tried it.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Do we need the names for it to work?

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Not technically. It would make follow-ups easier.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: It would also tell us quite a lot about where they are.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She leans back from the laptop. This is her favorite part of the work, and I've put a problem directly in it.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: I want the project to be useful. I don't want to build something so cautious it does nothing.

choices.text: Let's show both versions to the teacher before collecting anything.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: A review before a launch. Sensible, slightly less exciting.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: We could survive slightly less exciting.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: We keep saying that. Suspicious trend.

choices.text: We can test anonymous time bands first. Ask for more only if we can explain why.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: So we still test it. We just make the small version prove it needs to grow.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Exactly.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Aish. Fine. Good product advice. I reserve the right to grumble while I use it.

choices.text: People click through forms anyway. Add the names and launch it.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: That would be faster.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: And we can fix it later.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Unless what needs fixing is that people trusted us with too much.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: Teacher review is mandatory regardless of the choice. The approved pilot uses anonymous time bands and deletes test entries afterwards.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: I argued for speed. I still think speed matters.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: We can be quick about the things we understand.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: And careful about the things we don't. Okay. Put that in the notes before I make it sound like my idea.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: We arrive for a trial during a school network outage. Akira refreshes the page once, then makes herself stop.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: The internet is gone. Not slow. Gone. I'm taking this personally.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: It may not know we're here.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Then this is an appalling coincidence.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She checks the clock. The volunteer testers will arrive shortly.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: I could use my phone hotspot, but I don't know whether everyone will connect in time.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: What can we show without a connection?

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: The screen mock-ups. The anonymous totals. My ability to complain in several categories.

choices.text: Say the school broke our demo. That's basically true.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: The outage is real. Having no backup is ours.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Nobody asked for a backup.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: That's not a great reason to make the testers waste their time.

choices.text: We can postpone and explain why.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: I'll message the teacher and ask the testers which time works.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Better than making them wait for a loading screen.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: We are aggressively proving the need for good information.

choices.text: Let's run the test on paper. We're testing whether the information helps, right?

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Right. We don't need a network to ask a good question.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll get the prints.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: And I'll put 'paper' in the backup plan before I forget it exists again.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The teacher arranges a short paper check and a later digital trial. We spend the remaining block writing what failed and what still worked.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: I wanted a smooth demo.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: You got a useful test.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: I'm allowing myself five more minutes of being annoyed before I appreciate that.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Our project block overlaps with three requests from Akira's friends: a poster, a spreadsheet and a club signup page.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: They're all small. It's the combination that's developing teeth.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Have you agreed to all three?

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Technically, I said I could probably help.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: How did they hear that?

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: As yes. Correctly, to be fair.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She opens three message threads and can't seem to choose which one to answer.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: I like being someone people can count on. I don't want them to think that was fake.

choices.text: Tell them what you can finish and what you can't. You don't need a crisis to have a limit.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Even if someone is disappointed?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: They'll have better information than a late promise.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: You're using my own project against me. That's low. Also fair.

choices.text: Which one has the earliest real deadline?

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: The poster. The other two can wait if I actually say so.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Start with that message.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Right. One bridge at a time.

choices.text: If you want people around, doing them favors is part of the deal.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: I know I've said things like that.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You can't have it both ways.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Maybe I don't like what the deal turns me into.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: She sends three clear replies. One friend answers with a cheerful 'Next week is fine.' Another finds help elsewhere.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: Nobody has removed my name from the friendship register.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: There's a register?

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: No. Terrible privacy policy. We rejected it.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Akira has privately corrected the disclosure from the earlier survey session. The classmate agreed that she may discuss the lesson without sharing any more details.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: She heard my apology. She hasn't said she trusts me with personal stuff again.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: That might take time.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: I know. I nearly offered to fix her whole project to make it less awkward.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Did you?

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: No. I could practically hear the terrible bargain forming.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She has written 'Don't turn apology into sales pitch' at the top of her notebook.

choices.text: Give her some time. You don't need to solve it today.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: I'm bad at leaving things unfinished.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: She isn't a task.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Right. I'm glad you said that.

choices.text: If she accepted the apology, she should stop making it awkward.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: She didn't promise to make me feel better.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You admitted you were wrong.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: That was the part I owed her. It doesn't buy the next part.

choices.text: Keep doing what you promised, even when nobody thanks you for it.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: That sounds less satisfying than one big helpful gesture.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Probably.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Okay. Quietly reliable. I can be that. It'll be weird without a little success sound, but I'll cope.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We remove the last unnecessary personal fields from the pilot. Akira checks the consent text out loud before saving it.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: Will you tell me if I start dressing up a bad idea with enough enthusiasm to make it sound good?

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: I can try.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: Don't let me finish the whole presentation first. You'll be trapped here for hours.

warm.speaker: Akira
warm.text: I can say the embarrassing version to you. You don't seem to need the impressive one every time.

mixed.speaker: Akira
mixed.text: I'm still working out which of my clever ideas are actually excuses.

cool.speaker: Akira
cool.text: I want to be clear about this before we keep working. Private means private.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: While the prototype loads, a bright old pop song leaks from Akira's headphones. She hums the keyboard line before noticing.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You know the whole thing?

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: My mum plays it while she cooks. At this point it's part of the kitchen equipment.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You make the keyboard part sound easy.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: I learned it by getting it wrong a lot. Music is very efficient at telling you when you're wrong.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She taps the rhythm on the desk, then stops because another class is working nearby.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: I'll send you the song, if you want. No required essay afterwards.

choices.text: Send the one you like, not the one you think I'll like.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Dangerous. You might learn that I have embarrassing taste.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'm prepared for that risk.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Fine. The ridiculous opening stays. Don't blame me when you're humming it in maths. I warned you with my entire personality.

choices.text: Pick something more romantic. Then I might listen properly.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: You could listen because I wanted to share it.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I was trying to make that sound like a hint.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: It sounded like a condition.

choices.text: Sure. I don't know much music from that time.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Then I'll start with one song instead of twelve.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: A bold exercise in restraint.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Don't praise it until I actually press send.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We finish the loading test. My phone receives one song and, after a visible struggle across the desk, no long explanation.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: I want it on record that I had context ready.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: I believe you.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: Later, the chorus follows me all the way to the gate.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Teacher feedback is simple: keep the reliable pilot and drop the features we cannot maintain. Akira's original three-idea sheet sits beside the laptop.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: I wanted it to feel like the start of something big.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: It could still be a start.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: I know. I just liked the version where I got to show everybody I could do all of it.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She doesn't throw the sheet away. She folds it and puts it behind the current plan.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: My dad says opening a second shop won't fix the first one's broken fridge.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Your dad gets a lot of good lines.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Years of practice. Captive audience.

choices.text: We can keep the extra ideas in the report as future work.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Clearly marked as ideas. No accidental promises.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You've learned to fear that word.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: A healthy professional fear.

choices.text: Let's finish the version people can use without needing you beside it.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: A thing that works even when I'm not proving myself at it.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: That sounds like a good result.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Yeah. It does, actually. Let's make the instructions good.

choices.text: Keep the big features in the slides. We don't have to demonstrate them.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Then we'd be presenting something we don't have.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Everybody makes a project sound better.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: I'd rather make this one actually better.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We write a short maintenance guide and test it on someone who has never seen the prototype. Their first question reveals a button label neither of us understood.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: One word. We argued over the architecture and got beaten by one word.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Should we put that in the report?

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: Absolutely. It's the funniest useful thing we've learned.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: A few minutes after she leaves, I send a message: 'I'd like to spend time together when this is finished.' I stare at it for a while, then make myself put the phone away instead of adding three increasingly confusing explanations.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: During a lunch break from the final project checks, Akira asks about an earlier message from the MC.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: You wrote, 'I'd like to spend time together when this is finished.'

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I did.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: I nearly invited the whole project group. Then a friend said I should ask what you meant first.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She looks directly at me. No joke arrives to rescue either of us.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: I miss things when people expect me to understand a hint. I don't want to make you uncomfortable by guessing.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: She adjusts the little charm on her glasses, then deliberately puts both hands on the table. No escape into another explanation.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I'm glad you asked.

choices.text: I thought it was obvious. Everyone else figured it out.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: I didn't ask everyone else. I'm asking you.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: It just feels awkward explaining it.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: It's awkward being told I should already know.

choices.text: I meant just us. I'm interested in you, and I'd like to see whether you feel the same.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Okay. Thank you for saying it plainly.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: You don't have to answer while we're surrounded by lunch trays.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Good. I'd like to think without somebody asking me to pass the soy sauce.

choices.text: I was hoping for time with just you, but we can take it slowly.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: I can do slowly. I just need to know which conversation we're having.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: This one. No secret test.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Oh. Good. I was about to develop a flowchart for the hint. This is much nicer.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: We agree to finish the school handover first and speak privately afterwards. She doesn't promise a romantic answer.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: I do know that I want to be honest with you.

closing.speaker: Narration
closing.text: I can work with an honest answer. Waiting is harder, but it isn't unfair.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: The approved project is ready for its final class demonstration. Akira has written both names on the first slide.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: You remembered the paper backup.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: It has its own envelope. I have developed an emotional attachment.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: A tester asks a question Akira cannot answer immediately. She looks at the MC instead of filling the gap with a promise.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: We haven't tested that. Did we put it in the follow-up notes?

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: We did. It's still open.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She nods and writes down the question. Nothing collapses because she doesn't know everything.

choices.text: Let's explain the limits as clearly as the useful parts.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: 'Here's what it does. Here's what it doesn't.' That should fit on one slide.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: Your most ambitious small slide yet.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Don't tempt me. I'll add a graph.

choices.text: I'll handle the questions while you show the demo.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Deal. Stop me if I'm going too fast.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'll use the agreed hand signal.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: The normal one. Please. Not the dramatic throat-cutting thing from rehearsal; I thought the projector was dying.

choices.text: Promise the extra feature. We can work it out after they leave.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: No. I know how quickly 'later' turns into a pile of people waiting for me.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: It might win them over.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Then I'd be winning them over with something I haven't done.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: The handover ends with a working pilot, a short guide and a few useful questions. The class applauds briefly, then asks about homework.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: That's almost comforting. Our big moment and then algebra.

closing.speaker: MC
closing.text: Ordinary life continues.

closing.speaker: Akira
closing.text: Meet me in the canteen next time? Without bringing the laptop.

warm.speaker: Akira
warm.text: When I picture the demo going well, you're in the picture. That's been true for a while.

mixed.speaker: Akira
mixed.text: I've thought about what you said. I'd like to finish that conversation properly.

cool.speaker: Akira
cool.text: I want us to talk clearly about where we stand once the work is finished.

setup.speaker: Stage
setup.text: Finale encounter; show the route-ending warning first. The canteen is quiet after the supervised activity block. Akira has brought two canned coffees and no laptop.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: I chose these without a survey. Personal growth.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: Brave.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Before I make six jokes and accidentally avoid the point: I did think about us.

setup.speaker: Narration
setup.text: She turns the can between her hands. Her glasses charm taps softly against the frame.

setup.speaker: MC
setup.text: I still want to ask you out. Clearly, this time.

setup.speaker: Akira
setup.text: Then ask. I promise not to invite the whole class by accident.

choices.text: Would you like to spend Saturday together and see how it feels?

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: That's clear enough. I appreciate the lack of a five-year plan.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I barely have a Saturday plan.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Good place to start.

choices.text: I've waited while you figured it out. I need a yes now.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: You can ask for an answer. You can't choose which one I owe you.

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I didn't want to stay in the dark.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Then let me tell you the truth without trying to hurry it into something else.

choices.text: I'd like a date, just the two of us. Tell me what you actually want.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Even if it isn't the answer you're hoping for?

response.speaker: MC
response.text: I'd rather hear you than keep guessing.

response.speaker: Akira
response.text: Okay. Here goes.

closing.speaker: Stage
closing.text: Apply the final score once. Compare effective good and bad totals and play exactly one epilogue. Her answer is supplied by the ending, never by a shared acceptance line.

warm.speaker: Akira
warm.text: I've been looking forward to seeing you with nothing left to troubleshoot.

mixed.speaker: Akira
mixed.text: We got good at working together. This part needs its own answer.

cool.speaker: Akira
cool.text: I'm glad we finished the project. I need to be honest about the rest.

endings.title: Player Two
endings.cgBrief: A clean warm Class A project desk after school; pink-bobbed Akira with brown eyes behind glasses grins as she and the charcoal-silhouette MC place their hands together on a shared notebook. Simple completed demo on the nearby laptop, no readable text.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: I want that. A date. Just us. I tried practicing that without the giant smile, but the giant smile appears to be included.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Keep the smile. I like it.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: I like you, Ren. That's what I keep coming back to. No clever explanation. You, specifically. It's inconveniently hard to improve on.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: I had a good reply ready. It leaves my head before I can use it.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I like you too.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: Daebak. Okay. Excellent. Two people. Same answer. Why was that harder than the whole demo?

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Later, they return the project notebook to Class A. She leaves her hand on the cover beside his, then turns her palm upward. He takes it.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: Saturday. There's a café I'd like to show you. After that, maybe a walk. I will try not to turn it into a guided lecture.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: One topic allowed.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: You're negotiating with the wrong girl. One topic has subtopics, Ren. You should have read the small print.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: She's laughing now, but she isn't rushing past what happened. Neither am I. Saturday is a date, and today is the first time holding her hand feels simple enough to enjoy.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Akira / Good. Credits, then title.

endings.title: A Good Teammate
endings.cgBrief: Akira and the MC silhouette sit across a canteen table with the closed project notebook between them, warm ordinary daylight, friendly expressions and comfortable but distinct personal space.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: I like being with you. I don't feel the part I think you're asking for. I kept checking because I didn't want to give you the wrong answer.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Thanks for not giving me the easy one.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: I'm not sure there was an easy one.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: She slides the second coffee toward him and leaves her hand on her own side of the table.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: If being friends is difficult right now, you can say so. I won't turn it into an emergency project.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: A little difficult. I'd like to try, with some room to be awkward.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: Awkward I can handle. Unclear instructions are the real enemy.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: A week later, we have lunch with the project group. She asks before showing anyone a photo, then catches me noticing.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: What? Some features do make it into the final version.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I'm glad that one did.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: I don't secretly count the afternoon as progress toward changing her mind. We finished something useful together. I can let that be true without asking it to become something else.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Akira / Neutral. Credits, then title.

endings.title: Disconnect
endings.cgBrief: Akira alone at an ordinary Class A desk, short pink bob and glasses clear, closing a disconnected laptop; empty project chair beside her, expression thoughtful and resolved rather than shattered.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: I don't want to date you. I'm going to say that plainly, because I've spent too long hoping a softer version would make this easier.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I thought we were getting closer.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: Sometimes we were. Other times, I felt like being useful was the part of me you were waiting for. I don't want to build a relationship around that feeling.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: Her voice isn't loud. That makes it harder to pretend I misunderstood.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: All right. I'll give you space.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: Thank you. We can keep the handover polite. We don't have to pretend nothing happened.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: The following day, she closes the project laptop after returning the shared files. The spare chair stays pushed in.

lines.speaker: Narration
lines.text: The project will keep working without either of us beside it. I'm glad we managed that, even if I wish I'd handled the rest differently.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: Your copy is in the class folder. The instructions are on the first page.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: Got it. Good luck with the next idea.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: Thanks. I'm going to take a break before I start one.

lines.speaker: Stage
lines.text: Unlock Akira / Bad. Credits, then title.

lines.speaker: MC
lines.text: I shouldn't have pushed for a yes. I wanted an answer and got scared of the one I might hear.

lines.speaker: Akira
lines.text: Okay. I can hear the apology. Please don't make being clear mean agreeing with you. Let me choose my answer.
